questions.question: How does airline operation affect tourism revenue?
questions.solution_html:
• • Improved Accessibility
  • More flights and routes make destinations easier to reach, increasing tourist arrivals and
  • boosting spending on hotels, food, transport, and attractions.
  • • Lower Airfares
  • Competitive airline pricing encourages more people to travel, particularly for leisure
  • leading to higher tourism revenues.
  • • Increased Connectivity
  • Direct international flights connect remote or developing destinations to global tourism
  • markets, promoting regional economic growth.
  • • Seasonal and Charter Flights
  • Airlines can adjust operations to meet seasonal demand, ensuring a steady flow of
  • tourists during peak seasons.
  • • Cargo and Supply Support
  • Airlines also transport goods for the tourism industry—such as hotel supplies and food
  • products—supporting the overall tourism economy.
  • • Employment and Multiplier Effect
  • Airline operations create jobs and stimulate related sectors (hospitality, transport
  • retail), further increasing local income and government revenue.
questions.final_answer: retail), further increasing local income and government revenue

questions.question: Explain how airlines generate employment.
questions.solution_html:
• • Direct Employment
  • o Flight Crew: Pilots, co-pilots, and flight attendants are employed to operate and
  • manage flights.
  • o Ground Staff: Ticketing agents, check-in staff, baggage handlers, and security
  • personnel work at airports.
  • o Maintenance and Engineering: Technicians, engineers, and mechanics maintain
  • aircraft and ensure safety standards.
  • o Administrative Roles: Managers, accountants, HR personnel, and IT staff handle
  • airline operations and customer service.
  • • Indirect Employment
  • o Tourism and Hospitality: Airlines bring tourists who create demand for hotels
  • restaurants, travel agencies, and local guides.
  • o Airport Services: Jobs in catering, cleaning, fueling, and logistics arise from airline
  • operations.
  • o Manufacturing and Supply Chains: Aircraft manufacturing, parts suppliers, and
  • uniform or equipment providers also benefit.
  • • Induced Employment
  • o Income earned by airline and airport employees circulates through the economy
  • creating further jobs in retail, transport, and services.
questions.final_answer: creating further jobs in retail, transport, and services
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss the importance of hubs in global aviation networks.
questions.solution_html:
• • Efficient Connectivity
  • Hubs link multiple routes through a central point, allowing passengers to travel between
  • cities that may not have direct flights. This increases global connectivity.
  • • Cost Efficiency for Airlines
  • Concentrating flights at a hub allows airlines to maximize aircraft use, reduce operating
  • costs, and coordinate flight schedules more effectively.
  • • Increased Passenger Traffic
  • Hubs attract more travelers by offering convenient connections, boosting airport traffic
  • and local economic activity.
  • • Support for Global Alliances
  • Airline alliances (like Oneworld, Star Alliance, and SkyTeam) use hubs to coordinate
  • routes and offer seamless travel experiences across member airlines.
  • • Economic Development
  • Major hubs create employment, encourage tourism, and promote trade and investment
  • in the surrounding region.
  • • Cargo Handling and Logistics
  • Many hubs also serve as major centers for air cargo, facilitating international trade and
  • supply chain efficiency.
questions.final_answer: supply chain efficiency
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the responsibilities of airline staff in excess baggage handling.
questions.solution_html:
• • Weighing and Checking Baggage
  • Staff weigh each passenger’s luggage at the check-in counter and verify it against the
  • airline’s baggage allowance policy.
  • • Informing Passengers
  • They clearly explain baggage rules, including weight limits, size restrictions, and extra
  • charges for exceeding the allowance.
  • • Calculating Excess Baggage Fees
  • If the luggage exceeds the permitted limit, staff calculate the excess weight or additional
  • piece charges as per airline policy.
  • • Collecting Payment and Issuing Receipts
  • They collect payment for excess baggage and provide a valid receipt or baggage tag to
  • ensure transparency and tracking.
  • • Proper Tagging and Documentation
  • Staff attach excess baggage tags and ensure the items are correctly entered into the
  • airline’s system for tracking.
  • • Coordinating with Baggage Handlers
  • They inform ground handling staff about additional or heavy baggage to ensure proper
  • loading and weight distribution in the aircraft.
  • • Customer Assistance
  • If passengers need to remove or repack items, staff provide guidance or direct them to
  • repacking areas.
questions.final_answer: repacking areas
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain how AI improves flight efficiency.
questions.solution_html:
• • Optimized Flight Planning
  • AI analyzes weather data, air traffic, and fuel consumption patterns to plan the most
  • efficient routes, reducing flight time and fuel use.
  • • Predictive Maintenance
  • AI monitors aircraft systems and predicts potential mechanical issues before they occur.
  • This prevents delays, minimizes downtime, and lowers maintenance costs.
  • • Fuel Efficiency
  • Machine learning algorithms analyze data on engine performance, altitude, and wind
  • speed to suggest fuel-saving adjustments during flights.
  • • Air Traffic Management
  • AI assists in managing congested airspaces by predicting traffic flow and helping
  • controllers route aircraft more efficiently.
  • • Crew Scheduling
  • AI automates scheduling based on crew availability, qualifications, and legal limits
  • reducing human error and ensuring smooth operations.
  • • Passenger Flow and Check-in Automation
  • At airports, AI-driven systems like self-check-in kiosks and facial recognition reduce
  • waiting times and improve boarding efficiency.
  • • Data-Driven Decision Making
  • AI processes large volumes of operational data to help airlines make informed decisions
  • about fleet usage, scheduling, and demand forecasting.
questions.final_answer: about fleet usage, scheduling, and demand forecasting

questions.question: State two reasons why airlines insist on photo ID at check-in, with / examples.
questions.solution_html:
• • Passenger Identity Verification
  • To confirm that the person checking in is the same individual named on the ticket.
  • Example: Airlines like IndiGo or Air India verify an Aadhaar Card or Passport to match
  • the name on the booking.
  • • Security and Safety
  • Helps prevent unauthorized travel or misuse of tickets, ensuring that all passengers are
  • properly identified for security screening.
  • Example: As per DGCA (Directorate General of Civil Aviation) rules in India, passengers
  • must present valid ID before entering the airport terminal.
  • • Fraud Prevention
  • Prevents ticket fraud, impersonation, or identity theft, especially with e-tickets and
  • online check-ins.
  • Example: Airlines may reject boarding if the photo ID doesn’t match the name on the
  • ticket.
  • • Immigration and Legal Compliance
  • For international flights, airlines must verify identity documents to comply with
  • immigration and border control regulations.
  • Example: A Passport is mandatory for international travel.
  • • Record and Baggage Matching
  • Ensures baggage is checked in under the correct passenger name, which is crucial for
  • security tracking and lost luggage claims.
  • Example: A bag tag is issued only after photo ID verification.
questions.final_answer: Example: A bag tag is issued only after photo ID verification

  • speed to suggest fuel-saving adjustments during flights.
  • • Air Traffic Management
  • AI assists in managing congested airspaces by predicting traffic flow and helping

  • AI automates scheduling based on crew availability, qualifications, and legal limits
  • reducing human error and ensuring smooth operations.

  • At airports, AI-driven systems like self-check-in kiosks and facial recognition reduce
  • waiting times and improve boarding efficiency.

  • about fleet usage, scheduling, and demand forecasting.

questions.question: State two reasons why airlines insist on photo ID at check-in, with / examples.
questions.solution_html:
• • Passenger Identity Verification
  • To confirm that the person checking in is the same individual named on the ticket.
  • Example: Airlines like IndiGo or Air India verify an Aadhaar Card or Passport to match
  • the name on the booking.
  • • Security and Safety
  • Helps prevent unauthorized travel or misuse of tickets, ensuring that all passengers are
  • properly identified for security screening.
  • Example: As per DGCA (Directorate General of Civil Aviation) rules in India, passengers
  • must present valid ID before entering the airport terminal.
  • • Fraud Prevention
  • Prevents ticket fraud, impersonation, or identity theft, especially with e-tickets and
  • online check-ins.
  • Example: Airlines may reject boarding if the photo ID doesn’t match the name on the
  • ticket.
  • • Immigration and Legal Compliance
  • For international flights, airlines must verify identity documents to comply with
  • immigration and border control regulations.
  • Example: A Passport is mandatory for international travel.
  • • Record and Baggage Matching
  • Ensures baggage is checked in under the correct passenger name, which is crucial for
  • security tracking and lost luggage claims.
  • Example: A bag tag is issued only after photo ID verification.
